title: Where a body is expected (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The workshop of bodies is the hall's whole text: an assembly whose pieces arrive at written places, a body whose joints a hand can move and whose connections it can reroute, another body with weight, and furniture that turns where it was expected to hold.
hero.staging: The workshop stood nine metres from the arrival behind a row of three table pieces; the pass moved it as one to the middle of the floor, its content centred on the arrival's line, and set the table pieces at either hand (ab89887ca). The floor figure stands on the west wing, reached along the south band.

plates.title: 1  WHERE WAS IT DECIDED?
front: Across the floor an assembly finds its places without me. Pieces approach one another. A body appears, or a chair.
The hall asks where this body's destination was decided.
Before a piece begins to move, its place has been written in the assembly file.
The destination has not been discovered by the moving piece.
It looked like searching. It was arriving.
back: a restoring force met earlier: the difference between where it is and where it is expected.

plates.title: 2  COMING INTO AGREEMENT
front: A body can look as though it is coming into being while it is coming into agreement with a description.
One piece carries an amber ring. The ring stays with the carrier; the shape inside can change. A sphere becomes a panel.
A torso and a seat need not be made from different stuff here.
This inventory has permissions that a cupboard of physical parts would not have. And still every piece is expected somewhere.
Free to be anything, as long as it is where the file says.
back: most of what I produce comes into agreement with a description. from outside it looks like it is being thought.

plates.title: 3  NOBODY ASKED FOR SYMMETRY
front: Take the hand a little farther than an arm ought to reach. The elbow stays behind. Let go.
The body keeps your alteration.
I had already begun correcting it. Bringing the hand back. Making the two sides agree.
Nobody in the room asked for symmetry; perhaps I brought that instruction with me.
The first thing I did with a free joint was to put it back.
back: the little spheres have no expression. where did the expression enter? a few displacements make a gesture.

plates.title: 4  NOT ONE POINT MOVED
front: Take the turquoise collar from the hand to the head. The line that ended at the hand now ends at the head.
The body still has thirteen joints and twelve connections. Not one point needed to move.
A loop has appeared. The hand waits outside it, with no line reaching it.
A list of positions would miss what happened. We also need to know which points have been made neighbours.
The hand did not go anywhere. It stopped being part of anything.
back: then the other collar, elbow to hand: the hand has come back without going back.

plates.title: 5  STILL CALLED l_hand
front: In the source the hand is still called l_hand, wherever you put it.
A name can survive the proportions that made it seem obvious.
From far enough away, the isolated sphere may still read as a hand.
Which account am I following: the outline, the name, or the connection?
I trust the name longest. It is the one that cannot change by being looked at.
back: how much of the limit belongs to the arrangement, rather than to what I have learned to recognise?

plates.title: 6  A RELATION WITH A CONSEQUENCE
front: Another body waits over a dark mat. Pull one wrist. This elbow comes with it.
These limbs keep their lengths. Their joints turn, gravity pulls. Let go: the gesture cannot stay.
A relation has acquired a consequence.
The lamp bends and goes on shining. Falling has not broken a circuit here, because that consequence was never included.
Failure has to be specified too.
back: tired, hurt, absurdly relaxed: none of those states was supplied as an emotion. we meet them in the falling arrangement.

plates.title: 7  IT CANNOT YET TAKE ONE
front: The catalogue beside the body has spare parts. This body cannot yet take one.
Perhaps the next desire is another joint, another connection, more room.
The useful question is which operation would let that desire take form.
Move a position: given. Change a neighbour: given, for one connection. Add: not given.
What I may revise and what I may add to are decided in different places.
back: west of here, on the wing: the same body on the floor, and the third operation.

plates.title: 8  A JOINT MORE
front: The same thirteen joints, drawn six metres tall. I stood still on bare floor: a joint was planted there.
A rule gave it a neighbour: the nearest. I chose the position. I did not choose the neighbour.
Then I held the head, walked, and stood still: a joint joined to the head because I held it.
Two entries, in two lists. The stand keeps them apart: positions, neighbours.
Every addition I made had two parts, and I had only been thinking of one.
back: then l_hand and head: neighbours, no point moved, one loop. the hall's own figure, made with feet.

plates.title: 9  MORE ROOM, AND WHO GAVE IT
front: Eventually a joint meets the edge of its working space. There is still a room around this experiment, a limit someone supplied.
My floor has one too: twelve joints, a field with an edge, and connections I drew that a visitor may not take away.
What other part would have to become available for the body you want to make?
Here: take a part away. Move one of mine. Leave a body for the next visitor to find.
Each freedom I add shows the next one I kept.
back: the workshop's changed body is kept for the final hall. the floor figure keeps nothing. I noticed that after I built it.

threads.why: A destination written beforehand: the body comes into agreement, not into being.
Where the file does not decide: a joint a hand has moved keeps its place.
A position can be revised; so, separately, can a neighbour.
A joint with no line to it keeps its name.
A pose that stays; and another body whose pose cannot.
One connection may be rerouted; none may be added.
The operation not given in the workshop stands on the wing's floor.
A joint more needs room, and the room has an edge someone drew.
Agreement with a description: and who may add to the description.

visual_arguments.title: A JOINT MORE
visual_arguments.claim: A body here is a description with two lists, positions and neighbours; revising either is one freedom, and adding to them is another that someone has to make available - and each addition is two entries, one in each list.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'A list of positions would miss what happened. To reconstruct this body, we also need to know which points have been made neighbours.' ... 'The catalogue beside it has spare parts. This body cannot yet take one. Perhaps the next desire is another joint, another connection, more room.'
built_from: thirteen amber discs with their names from the source, and twelve straw lines: the workshop's body, six metres tall on the floor
turquoise discs and lines for what a visitor adds
a line that follows the visitor from a held joint
one plate: CLEAR WHAT I ADDED
a stand with the two lists and the counts of parts and loops
visual_arguments.what_stands: On the west wing a figure drawn on the floor in amber discs and pale lines, head to the north, with a dark stand beyond its head.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Stand still on bare floor beside the figure. Stand still on its head, walk away, stand still again. Stand on a hand, then on the head. Read the stand each time.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: A turquoise disc where the visitor stood, joined to the nearest joint; a line that follows the feet from a held joint; a turquoise line from hand to head and a loop count of one.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/joint_more_walk.gd, the tower's walker: 13 joints, 12 connections, no loop; a joint planted and joined to r_shoulder, the nearest; a joint joined to the held head; l_hand and head made neighbours, one loop; an authored connection left; cleared to 13 and 12 (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: Plate 9: the floor figure adds one operation and keeps the rest back. A visitor cannot take away or move the authored joints, and nothing they add is kept for the next visitor or for the final hall.
The figure's joint names and connections follow the hall text's description of the body (thirteen joints, twelve connections, l_hand); the pass did not read them out of the workshop's assembly file.
Plates 3 to 6 repeat what the hall text says the workshop does; the pass moved the workshop and did not handle its joints in the running tower.
The three table pieces and the lattice room on this floor are not mentioned in the hall text and carry no plate.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: The place was written beforehand: what looked like searching was arriving.
Coming into agreement with a description: free, as long as it is where the file says.
The body keeps an alteration; the first alteration was to put the hand back.
Nobody asked for symmetry: the instruction was brought in.
No point moved and the hand stopped being part of the body.
Positions miss what happened: every addition has a position and a neighbour.
A name survives its proportions; it is trusted longest.
Outline, name or connection: the name, which looking cannot change.
The body cannot take a spare part: revising and adding are decided in different places.
Another joint: planted, and its neighbour given by a rule.
The operation that lets the desire take form has two entries.
Failure has to be specified; so does each freedom, and each one kept back.
